What Is a Shim in mise? Shims | mise-en-place

A shim is a tiny executable that masquerades as the tool you want to run (e.g. node, prettier). Each shim is a symlink to the mise binary that intercepts your shell call, figures out which version of the tool should run, loads the declared mise/Environment changes, and then delegates execution. See Shims in the mise docs.

mise/activate rewrites Shell/PATH on every prompt; this is great for interactive shells but unavailable to non-interactive environments like CI, IDEs, or scripts. Shims offer a static directory of stand-ins that works even when the shell cannot evaluate mise activate. See Shims vs PATH activation.

By default, shims live in ~/.local/share/mise/shims. Adding this directory to PATH (or using mise activate --shims) makes every installed tool appear globally available. See mise activate --shims.
